alerts.reason: Douglas Dynamics attributed part of its 12.8% sales growth in 2021 to pent-up dealer demand and better snowfall in the season ended March 31 (A, D). I expect pricing to help keep March-quarter sales above the −5% threshold. April–June is the first full quarter after the snow season and compares against a year when dealers were catching up on purchases. I forecast a decline of at least 5% as that demand fades. The filing does not quantify how much catch-up buying occurred in that quarter.

Douglas Dynamics’ net sales fell 4.58% year over year in September and 3.30% in December. The annual totals in A and the quarterly figures imply first-half 2021 sales of about $261 million, up 39%. The 2020 shutdown began March 18 and disrupted second-quarter shipments (B, C), and dealers released pent-up demand in 2021 (D). I expect March to stay above −5% and the comparison with the spring 2021 rebound to push June to −5% or worse.

Pricing supported sales (D), but component shortages persisted into 2022 while backlog reached three to five times its usual size (B, C). I expect March growth to remain above −5% and delayed shipments against the stronger prior-year base to push June to −5% or worse.

Year-over-year growth narrowed from 7.49% to 0.84% (A). I expect its multiyear customer contracts (B) to cushion the slowdown enough to keep March above −5%, with further erosion taking June to −5% or worse.
